BPMN Activities

General Concept: BPMN Activities are elements that represent work performed in a process, such as Tasks, Subprocesses, and Call Activities. These elements manage execution, input/output mapping, and variable scoping, ensuring each activity is started, executed, and completed according to BPMN semantics and engine configuration.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
BPMN Activities in TaktX:

  • Support input and output variable mapping using FEEL expressions for flexible data transformation.
  • Allow for error handling, retries, and compensation, with boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling.
  • Provide hooks for monitoring, audit logging, and integration with external systems via the TaktX client.
  • Enable advanced features such as multi-instance execution, subprocess invocation, and user assignment.
  • Are specialized into concrete types (service, user, script, call, receive, etc.), each with unique options.

We recognise the following Activity subclasses 

  • External Tasks:
    • Service task 
    • Send task
    • Message End Event
    • Message Intermediate Throw Event
  • Script Tasks
  • User Tasks
  • Call Activities
  • Subprocesses
  • Receive Tasks
  • Generic Tasks

Markers

Each activity can have markers to add to specialized behaviour:

  • Multi-Instance Activities
  • Compensation (not supported yet)
